about: Scout reports as each release stored them (evidence/<run>/report.json, re-serialized from the parsed report) and as a scout writes one now. payload.title: Login flakes on CI
payload.summary: The login test races the session cookie.
payload.report:
## Findings

The test asserts before `Set-Cookie` arrives.

## Evidence

- `test/login.spec.ts:42` awaits navigation, not the cookie.

payload.title: Where the nightly export spends its time
payload.summary: Most of the 14 minutes is one unindexed query over events; the rest is gzip at level 9.
payload.report:
## Findings

1. `exportEvents` scans `events` without an index on `(project, at)`.
2. Compression runs at level 9 for a 2% gain.

## Risks

Adding the index locks the table briefly on large projects.

followUps.title: Index events by project and time
followUps.goal: The nightly export's events query uses an index on (project, at); export time on the fixture project drops below 5 minutes; a migration test covers the new index.

followUps.title: Compress exports at level 6
followUps.goal: Exports use gzip level 6; the export test asserts the level and the archive still round-trips.

payload.title: Ünïcode file names break the uploader
payload.summary: Names are normalised to NFD on macOS and compared as NFC on the server, so the same file uploads twice — e.g. “résumé.pdf”.
payload.report:
## Findings

```ts
const key = name.normalize("NFC");
```

The client never normalises; the server does. Café ≠ Café (NFD vs NFC).

## Evidence

— two uploads of `résumé.pdf` from one Mac produced rows 811 and 812.

followUps.title: Normalise upload names to NFC on the client
followUps.goal: The uploader normalises every file name to NFC before hashing and upload; a test uploads an NFD name twice and gets one row.
